newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Explorers Index continues to decline.
newsitem.headline: Australian Explorers Index continues to decline.

text.p: Perth stockbroker Eyres Reed Ltd said its Australian Explorers Index fell 117.9 points or 3.8 percent last week. The All Ordinaries Index rose 1.15 percent.
July 4 Jun 27 pct 1 Month pct 1 Year pct
NOTE: The explorers index (base 500, March 1992) tracks the performance of 88 small capitalisation exploration companies.
Eyres Reed analyst Glen Colgan said in a commentary that the index continued its lacklustre performance last week with bargain hunters initially bouncing prices higher after last week's tax sell-off.
This was before the gold bears took control, driving prices sharply lower as the bullion price faltered again.
The highlights of the week were the junior oil and gas stocks who found favour with punters as trading opportunities in other stocks dwindled. Falls putnumbered rises three to one.

Pan Pacific Petroleum NL lifted 7.5 cents to 27 cents, Carnarvon Petroleum NL up 0.5 cents to 3.3 cents, Stirling Resources NL rose 3.2 cents to 11.5 cents as did Stirling's largest shareholder Capital Energy NL, up 0.8 cents to 4.2 cents, and Austin Oil NL kicked strongly up 3.7 cents to 10.5 cents after a change of control.
The carnage in the gold sector spilled over to junior resource issues.

The largest falls included Consolidated Gold NL, down six cents to 26.5 cents, Goldstream Mining NL 7.5 cents lower at 39 cents, Border Gold NL drifted 3.5 cents to 19.5 cents, New Hampton Goldfields NL, off seven cents to 19 cents, Gindalbie Gold NL down four cents to 20 cents and Money Mining NL retreated four cents to 16 cents.
